subject: Random walk 2 for groups at irregular locations

messages.author: 3132b1ef78b4baf1
messages.subject: Random walk 2 for groups at irregular locations
parts:
Hi INLA group,

I am trying to fit a rw2 model through age-months grouped in the following 0, 1-11, 12-23, 24-35, 36-47, and 48-59. I was wondering what the best way to do this would be?

I know if i was to fit something like f(ageIndex, model = 'rw2') where ageIndex = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 for the six groups, this would not represent the different number of months in each group (1, 11, 12, 12, 12, 12), but I am unsure how to approach this. I thought about altering the constraint matrix by multiplying each row by 1/60, 11/60, 12/60, 12/60, 12/60, and 12/60, respectively, but i am not sure if this is the right thing to do?

If anyone had any advice on where to go with this, it would be very much appreciated!

Thanks in advance! 

Best,
Connor

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random walk 2 for groups at irregular locations
parts:
if you want to use one point for each group, then

f(idx, model="rw2", scale.model=TRUE, 
values= c(0,6,17.5,29.5, 41.5,53.5))

will do, then idx, for each index, should be one of the elements in
'values'.

make sure to use 'values' as the x-axis in plotting...
